model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net_debt = 0

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $235M; TTM to 2026-06-30 estimated at ~$240M (no interim XBRL tag). Bank SBC is a real compensation cost and is charged in the flows via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,558.05M common shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 (10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding); Q2-26 weighted diluted 1,555M, dilutive securities immaterial (~1M options, ~9M unvested RSUs largely in the treasury-method count). Includes the 6.6M shares issued for BTIG on 2026-06-01. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows and buybacks are a use of the FCFE already being valued.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest, post-preferred FCFE. US 10y ~4.2% + beta ~1.05 x 5.5% ERP = ~10.0%. Base 10.0% (USB is a higher-quality, lower-loss-history franchise than TFC at 10.5%); bull 9.75%; bear 10.5% (credit path already carries most of the bear, so only +50bp to avoid charging risk twice).
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a -- bank; occupancy cost is inside noninterest expense, no lease charge modelled separately.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI ($463M equity, ~$24M/yr income) and preferred dividends (~$371M/yr TTM incl. participating-securities allocation) are removed INSIDE the flow: the 'EBITDA' line is pre-tax income less a pre-tax-equivalent of pref dividends + NCI income, so the after-tax flow is net income to COMMON. Preferred is therefore NOT also deducted in the equity bridge (doing both would charge it twice).
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent TFC, HBAN, NTRS, STT, NAB.AX; SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book -- FCFE-at-CoE with retention = growth x regulatory capital is the equivalent flow form and keeps USB comparable with the other US banks in this folder). Engine mapping: revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, $29,583M TTM; the XBRL 'Revenues' tag / CSV Revenue column is $29,694M, ~0.4% higher, and is not used); 'ebitda' = pre-tax income + SBC - pre-tax-equivalent(pref dividends + NCI income) = $9,958M = 33.66% of revenue TTM; D&A 0; 'capex' = capital retention required to grow CET1 with the balance sheet = revenue x CET1/revenue (1.646) x g/(1+g); wc 0; net_debt 0 (deposits and wholesale debt are operating funding). TTM build: pre-tax 10,204 = revenue 29,583 - noninterest expense 17,117 - provision 2,262; tax 2,012 (19.7%); NI 8,168; NI to common 7,797. CET1 capital ~$48.7B = 10.8% x RWA ~$451B (RWA backed out of TCE/RWA 9.4%); TCE $42.4B (equity 67,432 - preferred 6,808 - goodwill 13,234 - other intangibles 4,999), AOCI -$7,111M. last_fcf 5,470 = NI to common 7,797 less retention to grow CET1 at the TTM loan-growth-adjusted 5% (~$2.3B): an FCFE proxy, since bank OCF is meaningless. Equity bridge: BTIG contingent cash consideration (up to $275M over 3 years). Excess CET1: none credited -- CET1 is 10.8% at both Dec-25 and Jun-26, management runs it flat, and the March 2026 capital proposals are 'expected to be favorable' but unquantified. Upside not in the model: AOCI pull-to-par and any capital relief from the 2026 rule proposals.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.note: Q2-26 10-Q: up to $275M payable over three years on performance targets; deducted at the maximum

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.1% vs EPS 5yr 8.6% -- >30% divergence. Book value is distorted by the 2022 AOCI hit (rate shock on the securities book) and the Dec-2022 MUFG Union Bank acquisition (44M shares issued; inflates the 3yr revenue CAGR too). FY2020 EPS is a COVID-provision trough, flattering the 5yr EPS CAGR. Revenue 5yr CAGR selected as the cleanest organic anchor.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_*_cagr fields carry NET INCOME TO COMMON CAGRs (FY2022 5,501 / FY2020 4,621 -> FY2025 7,194): bank OCF/FCF swings with trading assets and loans held for sale and is not an owner cash flow. Both NI endpoints are depressed (2022 Union Bank integration costs, 2020 reserve build).

base.margin_rationale: Year 1 delivers the Investor Day framework of 200bp+ positive operating leverage: revenue +5%, expense +3% takes the efficiency ratio from 57.9% (TTM GAAP) to ~56.8%; provision held ~7.6% of revenue (NCOs 0.53%). Margin then matures by year 4 at ~36% (efficiency ~55.5%, provision drifting up to ~8% of revenue as credit normalises). Implied return on TCE ~19.5% terminal vs 18.7% Q2-26 -- inside the 18%+ target, not above it.
base.capex_rationale: Retention = CET1/revenue 1.646 x g/(1+g): keeps CET1 at 10.8% as RWA grows with revenue.

bear.margin_rationale: Year-2 recession: provision roughly doubles to ~14% of revenue (NCOs ~1.0%, CRE office + card), NII squeezed by rate cuts; margin recovers to 33% -- below today's because the efficiency programme stalls (efficiency ~58%).

scenario_narratives.base: USB grinds out the 2025 Investor Day framework: 4-6% revenue growth as fixed-rate securities and swaps keep repricing into NII (NIM 2.79% in Q2-26, rising), payments (Elavon merchant acquiring, card) and the newly acquired BTIG lift fee income, and expense discipline delivers ~200bp of operating leverage until the efficiency ratio settles near 55-56%. Credit stays benign-to-normalising (NCOs ~0.5-0.6%), CET1 is run flat at ~10.8% and everything above the capital needed for growth goes out as dividends and buybacks. Return on tangible common settles ~19%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate-neutral balance sheet plus continued asset repricing push NII growth above the range; payments re-accelerates as Elavon's integrated-software channel scales; BTIG and the capital-markets build add a durable fee leg; and the March-2026 capital proposals land 'favorable' as management expects, letting USB hold less capital per dollar of RWA. Efficiency reaches ~53-54%, ROTCE ~21%, and the market pays a premium-regional multiple again.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2027-28 US recession: loan growth stalls, Fed cuts compress deposit spreads faster than assets reprice, card and CRE-office losses push provisions to ~1% of loans, and the efficiency programme stalls under BTIG and technology spend. USB stays well-capitalised (no solvency case -- CET1 10.8%, diversified fee base), but earnings power resets lower and the market caps it like a sub-par regional.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): credit is late-cycle, the ACL scenario set runs unemployment to 9.5% in its downside, and bank earnings are levered to it -- but there is no solvency or funding axis. Base 55%: Q2-26 delivered the framework (operating leverage, ROTCE 18.7%). Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both a capital-rule windfall and sustained above-range NII growth, two independent things.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what common shareholders can take out: net income to common less the earnings that must be retained to keep CET1 at 10.8% as the balance sheet grows, discounted at the cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale debt are operating funding, so there is no net-debt deduction; preferred dividends and NCI are removed inside the flow.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: provision is ~7.6% of revenue today; a 1% NCO year takes ~$2B pre-tax out of one year's earnings (bear case).
Rate path: NII repricing tailwind assumes the fixed-rate book keeps rolling at higher yields; faster Fed cuts compress deposit spreads.
Capital rules: the March-2026 proposals are 'expected to be favorable' but unquantified; AOCI (-$7.1B) inclusion in CET1 under any revived Basel endgame would raise retention needs.
Retention ratio: CET1/revenue 1.646 is backed out of reported ratios (TCE/RWA 9.4%, CET1 10.8%), not a disclosed RWA figure.
Terminal value ~55-65% of value; the 15x FCFE cap and 3% terminal growth carry it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 45.02-66.08
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK 36104 (InterestIncomeExpenseNet, NoninterestIncome, pre-tax income, tax, NI to common, preferred carrying value, goodwill/intangibles, diluted shares); Q2-2026 10-Q (usb-20260630.htm, filed 2026-08-06) for CET1 10.8%, TCE/RWA 9.4%, efficiency 57.1%, ROTCE 18.7%, AOCI, BTIG terms, 2026 capital proposals; USB_Metrics.csv for history.
data_sources.qualitative: Q2-2026 10-Q MD&A; 2025 Investor Day medium-term targets (4-6% revenue growth, 200bp+ operating leverage, 18%+ ROTCE). No USB_Analysis.json existed at build time.
